Tells a real tactic from a pattern whose key square is covered or undefended
Says when a position is quiet and no tactic exists

steps.text:
Before you play a clever-looking move, check that a tactic exists at all. Many positions have none.
List your **checks, captures and threats**. For each, ask what your opponent's best reply is, above all whether the piece you moved can simply be taken.

steps.caption: White to move. A pawn can fork the king and the rook, but look at the square.

line.say: The pawn gives check and attacks the rook.
The king takes the pawn. Nothing defended f4.

claims.statement: f4+ gains nothing along the engine line: the king takes the pawn.

steps.text:
A pattern on the board is not a tactic until it passes three checks.
**Can the piece I move be taken?** A covered square ruins a fork.
**Does the target really fall** after the best reply?
**Is a quiet move better?** If no forcing move works, improve your worst piece.

steps.title: The pattern is there, the tactic is not
steps.prompt: A black pawn stands on c6 in the second position.
Before each position, did you expect a tactic to exist? How often were you right?

steps.text: **Remember.** Many positions have no tactic, so check before playing a clever-looking move. List checks, captures and threats and ask for the best reply. A pattern is a tactic only if the moved piece cannot be taken and the target really falls. If nothing works, improve your worst piece.
